findings.text: Host early setup exposes an init routine that discovers the TDX private KeyID interval, reserves the first ID for module metadata, publishes guest range and count, enables the host platform capability, checks errata, registers a memory online gate, and refuses to proceed when KeyIDs are too few or hibernation remains available.

A machine-check helper classifies a fault as TDX private memory only when the record carries a usable memory address and the address queries as private; otherwise it reports no match. This isolates TDX attribution from generic memory error handling.
Module metadata access exposes a getter that returns null until initialization completes and thereafter returns a stable pointer to collected system info, plus a getter for the guest KeyID count.
Guest KeyID management exposes allocation within a fixed contiguous interval starting after the global ID and release back to the same pool, providing unique IDs for trust domains.

Trust domain lifecycle wrappers expose creation and key operations keyed by the trust domain root physical address: create with a hardware KeyID, configure key, initialize with parameters and extended status, finalize measurement, flush virtual processors, confirm flush completion, and release the KeyID.

Secure page and control-structure wrappers expose adding extra control pages, adding measured pages with a source page, adding secure page-table pages, augmenting pages dynamically, blocking an address range, extending measurement, removing pages, reclaiming physical pages with type owner and size outputs, and reading or writing management and virtual-processor fields.

Virtual processor wrappers expose creation bound to a trust domain root, attaching extra control pages, initializing with an initial register value and x2APIC ID, and entering the guest with caller supplied module arguments.

Global KeyID configuration happens at most once per physical package and invocations are serialized across CPUs, with system-wide cache invalidation beforehand to make prior unprotected PAMT copies visible before protected access.
Trust domain root addressing is derived from the stored root page for every management call, so all operations on one domain share a single stable root identifier.
Pages handed to the secure module are flushed from cache beforehand for create and add style calls, preserving coherence between normal and protected views of the same physical page.
Secure page-table level supplied to the module is one less than the host page-table level, with the empty level treated as invalid.

Private-address classification queries the module for page type: unassociated means shared, reserved means private only when inside a PAMT range, any other type means private, and any query failure or missing host support means shared.
PAMT membership is decided by range containment against each consumed TDMR PAMT interval, treating the TDMR list as immutable after module readiness.
Module enablement requires host platform support plus XSAVE, MOVDIR64B and self-snoop capabilities; absence of any prerequisite aborts initialization before changing global state.
Memory hotplug policy is static: an empty tracking list permits all online events, otherwise only a range fully contained in one tracked entry is permitted and anything else is rejected.
KeyID partitioning requires at least one reported TDX ID to proceed, and overall enablement requires at least two so one can serve module metadata and at least one remains for guests.
System metadata collection chains subqueries so a failure short-circuits later reads, and CPUID configuration counts are validated against local storage capacity before indexed reads.
Extended error reporting convention returns primary status as the call result while copying module-provided detail registers into caller outputs for page, range, measurement and init operations.
Construction of the TDX usable-memory list holds the online-memory read lock, matching the hotplug notifier path that consults the same list when deciding whether new memory may come online.
Readers of the consumed TDMR list issue a read barrier before traversal, relying on publication before module readiness and read-only use afterwards rather than a lock.

Collected system info aggregates version, feature flags, TDMR sizing limits and PAMT entry sizes, control-structure base sizes, and trust-domain configurability including attribute and extended-feature masks plus variable CPUID leaves and values.
TDMR bookkeeping exposes per-region base and size with a consumed count, and PAMT location is retrievable per region for range checks and teardown accounting.
Tracked usable memory is a list of entries carrying start and end page frame numbers, checked by containment for hotplug decisions.

Module call arguments convey guest address combined with level, domain or processor identifiers, source or destination physical addresses, field selectors with data and mask, and return field contents or reclaimed-page attributes through fixed registers.

Module initialization advances through capability discovery, compatibility validation, usable-memory enumeration, TDMR allocation and coverage, module configuration with the global KeyID, per-package key setup, and per-TDMR initialization, unwinding allocations and resetting PAMT state on failure.
Each TDMR is initialized incrementally: repeated module calls resume from a module-supplied next address with voluntary rescheduling until the cursor reaches the end of the region.

Host enablement progresses from feature checks to CPU hotplug registration, then module initialization, then suspend-callback registration and publication of readiness; failure removes the hotplug registration and leaves the module unmarked.

Early boot entry records partitioning, blocks on too few IDs or hibernation, registers the memory gate, disables suspend-to-RAM where applicable, assigns global and guest KeyID ranges, and marks host capability plus errata.
Hotplug entry filters only going-online transitions through the static TDX memory policy and leaves all other notifications unaffected.
Skipping system-wide cache invalidation before first protected PAMT access or before returning partially initialized PAMT memory can leave stale unprotected copies and corrupt metadata handling.
Running key configuration concurrently or more than once per package risks module errors; serialization and per-package deduplication are required.

Affected server CPU generations require forced bug flags for partial writes to private memory causing later machine checks and for VMCS loss across secure-loader calls without the hardware no-invalidation indication.
Suspend to RAM and hibernation are incompatible with an enabled module in these paths; suspend entry is cleared and hibernation availability aborts setup.
KeyID partitioning control reports MKTME count in the low half and TDX private count in the high half, with TDX IDs starting immediately after the MKTME range.

Global metadata selectors identify feature flags, TDMR limits and PAMT entry sizes, control-structure sizes, configurability masks, vCPU limits and CPUID tables, including indexed leaves and paired values.
Virtual-processor initialization carries an explicit interface version selecting APIC ID support, distinct from unversioned management calls.
